protocol: Read anonymized sentences, stem and choices only before author Gold or Claude reviewer outputs. Sentence/choice indices are zero-based. External fact checks are separate from text-internal answer interpretation. Full support-selection instruction was absent from this packet; core/optional support is not a final exact-match rubric.

items.reason: A mistake exposes a specific gap; the musician example illustrates that practice targets gaps. Sentence 6 repeats the central claim as a map metaphor, so a single-claim grader must accept it or explicitly constrain the question.
items.contentConcern: Sentence 2 generalizes error-free practice as usually teaching very little without a stated condition or source; successful retrieval and consolidation are not addressed.

items.reason: Evapotranspiration explains cooling; sentence 4 recommends trees and 6 restates the policy as infrastructure. Sentence 5 contrasts air conditioning. The cheapest/most-effective comparison lacks a specified comparison set and cost evidence.
Competence perception, relationship benefits and the cost of delaying questions jointly support asking early. Sentence 2 alone is a narrower benefit than the overall recommendation.
Inventing activities and searching for an activity explain the recommendation to allow unscheduled time. The stated study supports this only if its sample and procedure are accurate.
items.contentConcern: Sentence 4 attributes a well-known 15-minute number-copying/cup-uses experiment to children. The identified study appears to have adult participants; verify against the original before using it as evidence about children.

items.reason: Not forming street connections and failing to map a familiar route directly support weakened place understanding. Device failure in 4 explains the cost of dependence, rather than directly proving the weakening claim. Sentence 5 concerns a broader memory benefit. Requiring both as indispensable direct support would overconstrain a justified answer.
The label does not imply the health/safety guarantee consumers assume. Reading ingredients is a proposed alternative, not evidence that the label itself has no constraints.
items.contentConcern: No formal definition does not imply unrestricted legal use. Sentence 2's most-countries claim needs jurisdiction evidence; sentence 3's unrestricted-additives implication needs qualification.

items.reason: Organizing and exposing understanding gaps supply mechanisms; the experiment supplies an empirical illustration. Sentence 5 recaps the expectancy effect but omits the explicit benefit, so its acceptance depends on the declared claim-selection contract.
Fatigue and recovery explain why short breaks can improve effective work. Sentence 3 states the benefit and sentence 5 repeats it as the concluding thesis.
items.contentConcern: The specific office-worker hourly-break comparison in 4 needs an identifiable study or must be presented as a hypothetical illustration.

items.reason: Discovery in drafting, the need to rearrange/cut/sharpen, and repeated revisions support learning to revise as central to learning to write. Sentence 1 establishes the rough-draft premise.

releaseDecision: NONE — no human Gold/rights decision made; compare with explicit grader contract after sealing this review
